scenes.tts: Where do the enzymes go? This yeast mutant keeps making them at thirty-seven degrees. But it releases little.
scenes.caption: Where do the enzymes go? This yeast mutant keeps making them at 37 °C. But it releases little.
scenes.visual: THE WORLD, built once and kept all film: one yeast cell in cross-section filling about 80% of frame height. Left: ER as folded GREY sheets. Centre: Golgi as a few dispersed, unstacked GREY cisternae (yeast Golgi is not a stack). Right: the cell surface, a thick GREY arc. Top-left: a thermometer chip reading '37 °C' in RED. Top-right: a vertical bar gauge 'enzyme inside' marked 'schematic'. Bottom: an empty strip with three unlit lamps (lit later). Show first: ORANGE enzyme dots keep appearing at the ER, ride YELLOW vesicles rightward, and crowd up inside the cell near the surface arc, not shown attached to it; few cross it. The gauge climbs. On 'Where do the enzymes go?' a question 'Where do they go?' sits above the pile.
scenes.narration: Where do the enzymes go? This yeast mutant keeps making them at 37 °C. But it releases little.

scenes.visual: Title 'Three Handoffs for a Vesicle' over the dimmed cell; the YELLOW vesicles keep jostling in their pile so the frame never freezes.

scenes.tts: Yeast secrete enzymes along a route: E R, then Golgi, then vesicles, then the cell surface. Small membrane spheres called vesicles carry the cargo.
scenes.caption: Yeast secrete enzymes along a route: ER, then Golgi, then vesicles, then the cell surface. Small membrane spheres called vesicles carry the cargo.
scenes.visual: Thermometer turns to '25 °C' in TEXT colour; the pile clears. A dashed GREY arrow traces the route ER to Golgi to surface (labels 'ER', 'Golgi', 'surface' appear as the arrow reaches each). A YELLOW vesicle with ORANGE dots buds from the ER, rides to the Golgi and merges; another buds from the Golgi, rides to the surface and fuses with it (its membrane merging into the surface arc), and ORANGE dots are released outside. This loop keeps running slowly under the narration. Gauge stays low.
scenes.narration: Yeast secrete enzymes along a route: ER, then Golgi, then vesicles, then the cell surface. Small membrane spheres called vesicles carry the cargo.

scenes.tts: This mutant is called sec one. At twenty-five degrees it grows and secretes. At thirty-seven degrees, its enzyme pool inside rises up to eightfold.
scenes.caption: This mutant is called sec1. At 25 °C it grows and secretes. At 37 °C, its enzyme pool inside rises up to eightfold.
scenes.visual: Label 'sec1' appears on the cell outline. At 25 °C the loop from s02 keeps running. Thermometer slides to '37 °C' in RED. Vesicles still bud and travel, but pile up inside the cell near the surface, not shown attached to it (whether they were caught is unknown). The gauge climbs to a top tick labelled 'up to 8×'; the rest of the gauge stays 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: This mutant is called sec1. At 25 °C it grows and secretes. At 37 °C, its enzyme pool inside rises up to eightfold.

scenes.tts: The enzymes sit in membrane-bound vesicles that fail to fuse with the surface. Back at twenty-five degrees, with protein synthesis blocked, the cells secrete them.
scenes.caption: The enzymes sit in membrane-bound vesicles that fail to fuse with the surface. Back at 25 °C, with protein synthesis blocked, the cells secrete them.
scenes.visual: Camera eases toward the pile: YELLOW vesicles full of ORANGE dots inside the cell near the surface arc, with no attachment shown. Thermometer back to '25 °C'. A cell-wide label 'protein synthesis blocked' appears (no X on any organelle), and no new ORANGE dots form anywhere. The piled vesicles now fuse with the surface one by one, ORANGE dots spill outside, and the gauge falls. Camera eases back out.
scenes.narration: The enzymes sit in membrane-bound vesicles that fail to fuse with the surface. Back at 25 °C, with protein synthesis blocked, the cells secrete them.

scenes.tts: Every vesicle on that route has three jobs. Budding: pick up cargo and pinch off. Targeting: be caught by the right membrane. Fusion: merge with it.
scenes.visual: One vesicle replays its last trip, Golgi to surface, in slow motion. As it pinches off the Golgi, the first lamp in the bottom strip lights GREEN and its label 'budding' appears; as it is held at the surface, the second lamp lights ('targeting'); as it merges, the third lights ('fusion'). The strip stays on screen for the rest of the film.
scenes.narration: Every vesicle on that route has three jobs. Budding: pick up cargo and pinch off. Targeting: be caught by the right membrane. Fusion: merge with it.

scenes.tts: Back to sec one. For the last vesicle on the route, which job worked? And which could have failed?
scenes.caption: Back to sec1. For the last vesicle on the route, which job worked? And which could have failed?
scenes.visual: Thermometer to '37 °C' RED; the pile re-forms inside the cell near the surface (no attachment shown) and the gauge rises again. The three lamps dim. Question card above the pile: 'Which job worked? Which failed?'
scenes.narration: Back to sec1. For the last vesicle on the route, which job worked? And which could have failed?

scenes.visual: Predict pause. The question card stays. The piled vesicles jostle gently; the lamps pulse dimly in turn.

scenes.tts: Budding worked, because the vesicles exist. Targeting or fusion failed. A pile of vesicles alone cannot tell you which.
scenes.visual: The 'budding' lamp turns GREEN with a check. One RED bracket with a single question mark spans both the 'targeting' and 'fusion' lamps; neither lamp is marked on its own.
scenes.narration: Budding worked, because the vesicles exist. Targeting or fusion failed. A pile of vesicles alone cannot tell you which.

scenes.tts: Budding first. A coat of proteins assembles on a patch of membrane. Think of a cookie cutter with hands: it bends a bud and grabs the cargo.
scenes.visual: Camera pushes into the ER edge of the same cell (the lamps stay at the bottom). BLUE coat pieces (labelled shapes, no structures) settle on the cytosol side of the GREY membrane. The membrane bows outward into a bud. Small BLUE 'hands' reach the tails of membrane-spanning cargo carriers, and ORANGE cargo gathers inside the bud. Label 'coat' appears after the bud has formed.
scenes.narration: Budding first. A coat of proteins assembles on a patch of membrane. Think of a cookie cutter with hands: it bends a bud and grabs the cargo.

scenes.tts: At the E R this coat is COP two. A switch called Sar one, holding GTP, pulls it on. When Sar one hydrolyzes that GTP, the coat begins to let go.
scenes.caption: At the ER this coat is COPII. A switch called Sar1, holding GTP, pulls it on. When Sar1 hydrolyzes that GTP, the coat begins to let go.
scenes.visual: A BLUE shape labelled 'Sar1' with a GREEN 'GTP' badge sits at the bud neck; the coat label becomes 'COPII'. The bud pinches off as a YELLOW vesicle. The badge flips to GREY 'GDP' and BLUE coat pieces begin to peel away and drift off.
scenes.narration: At the ER this coat is COPII. A switch called Sar1, holding GTP, pulls it on. When Sar1 hydrolyzes that GTP, the coat begins to let go.

scenes.tts: In a test tube, vesicles made with a GTP analogue that cannot be hydrolyzed still budded. But they kept their coat, and failed to target and fuse. Making a vesicle and delivering it are separate steps.
scenes.visual: A dashed outline labelled 'cell-free' encloses the ER and Golgi. The badge now reads 'GTP analogue' with a lock; it never flips. A new vesicle buds (first lamp GREEN) but keeps its full BLUE coat, drifts near the Golgi and stays uncaught and unmerged. The second lamp turns RED. The dashed outline fades as the scene ends.
scenes.narration: In a test tube, vesicles made with a GTP analogue that cannot be hydrolyzed still budded. But they kept their coat, and failed to target and fuse. Making a vesicle and delivering it are separate steps.

scenes.tts: Here is the one idea. A vesicle's trip is three handoffs, and each can fail on its own. A coat buds it. A Rab and a tether catch it. SNAREs, guided by an S M protein, fuse it.
scenes.caption: Here is the one idea. A vesicle's trip is three handoffs, and each can fail on its own. A coat buds it. A Rab and a tether catch it. SNAREs, guided by an SM protein, fuse it.
scenes.visual: Camera pulls back to the whole cell at '25 °C'. One vesicle makes the Golgi-to-surface trip, and at each handoff a labelled shape passes it on while its lamp lights GREEN: BLUE 'coat' at the Golgi, TEAL 'Rab + tether' linking the vesicle to the surface (Rab on the vesicle), PURPLE 'SNAREs + SM protein' as it merges. The sentence 'Three handoffs. Each can fail alone.' appears at the top and stays until s13.
scenes.narration: Here is the one idea. A vesicle's trip is three handoffs, and each can fail on its own. A coat buds it. A Rab and a tether catch it. SNAREs, guided by an SM protein, fuse it.

scenes.tts: Targeting next. A Rab is a small switch with a lipid tail. Holding GDP, it can be carried in the cytosol by G D I. At the right membrane, an exchange factor loads GTP, and the Rab holds on.
scenes.caption: Targeting next. A Rab is a small switch with a lipid tail. Holding GDP, it can be carried in the cytosol by GDI. At the right membrane, an exchange factor loads GTP, and the Rab holds on.
scenes.visual: Camera pushes into a secretory vesicle approaching the surface (in this route the Rab rides on the vesicle). A TEAL flag labelled 'Rab' with a short lipid tail rides in the cytosol tucked inside a PINK cup labelled 'GDI', carrying a GREY 'GDP' badge. At the vesicle membrane the tail slips into the bilayer and the PINK cup drifts away. A small shape labelled 'exchange factor' swaps the badge to GREEN 'GTP'; the flag brightens and stays planted.
scenes.narration: Targeting next. A Rab is a small switch with a lipid tail. Holding GDP, it can be carried in the cytosol by GDI. At the right membrane, an exchange factor loads GTP, and the Rab holds on.

scenes.tts: Rab with GTP is one lit sign over a loading bay. It recruits tethers, which catch the vesicle. It is one sign among several.
scenes.visual: The lit TEAL flag glows like a sign. A preformed TEAL tether complex (a multi-part shape, not a growing rod) binds the lit flag on the vesicle and the surface membrane, drawing the vesicle near; the 'targeting' lamp lights GREEN. On 'one sign among several', two other spots glow briefly: a small lipid patch in the membrane and the SNARE stubs (next scene).
scenes.narration: Rab with GTP is one lit sign over a loading bay. It recruits tethers, which catch the vesicle. It is one sign among several.

scenes.tts: Fusion last. Two membranes resist merging, so SNARE proteins supply the pull. Four strands, called Q a, Q b, Q c and R, come from the two membranes.
scenes.caption: Fusion last. Two membranes resist merging, so SNARE proteins supply the pull. Four strands, called Qa, Qb, Qc and R, come from the two membranes.
scenes.visual: Close on the gap between the caught vesicle and the surface; a thin shimmer in the gap shows the membranes pushing back. Four PURPLE strands from three proteins: one strand anchored in the surface membrane ('Qa'), a single protein lying on the surface side that contributes two linked strands ('Qb', 'Qc') with no membrane-spanning anchor, and one strand anchored in the vesicle ('R'). Labels appear after the strands settle. Label 'SNAREs'.
scenes.narration: Fusion last. Two membranes resist merging, so SNARE proteins supply the pull. Four strands, called Qa, Qb, Qc and R, come from the two membranes.

scenes.tts: They zip into one rope, toward the membrane anchors. The zipping pulls the two bilayers together until they fuse. The zip itself uses no ATP.
scenes.visual: The four PURPLE strands (Qb and Qc still linked) twist together starting at the end farthest from the membranes and zip down toward them; the vesicle is drawn in, the two GREY membranes merge, and ORANGE cargo spills outside. The 'fusion' lamp lights GREEN. A GOLD 'ATP' badge appears beside the zip and is crossed out.
scenes.narration: They zip into one rope, toward the membrane anchors. The zipping pulls the two bilayers together until they fuse. The zip itself uses no ATP.

scenes.tts: In the main fusion steps studied, SNAREs also need an S M protein. It binds them and helps the right four zip together.
scenes.caption: In the main fusion steps studied, SNAREs also need an SM protein. It binds them and helps the right four zip together.
scenes.visual: A second caught vesicle; a PURPLE-outlined symbol labelled 'SM protein' sits with the assembling SNAREs as they zip (schematic help; no specific binding geometry drawn). Fusion again; cargo spills out.
scenes.narration: In the main fusion steps studied, SNAREs also need an SM protein. It binds them and helps the right four zip together.

scenes.tts: Sec one is the S M protein for the last step of secretion. That step is fusion of secretory vesicles with the plasma membrane.
scenes.caption: Sec1 is the SM protein for the last step of secretion. That step is fusion of secretory vesicles with the plasma membrane.
scenes.visual: Camera pulls back to the whole cell. The SM symbols at the surface gain the label 'Sec1'. The RED question-mark bracket from s08, which spanned 'targeting' and 'fusion', shrinks onto the 'fusion' lamp alone.
scenes.narration: Sec1 is the SM protein for the last step of secretion. That step is fusion of secretory vesicles with the plasma membrane.

scenes.tts: So at thirty-seven degrees, vesicles still bud and pile up. Back at twenty-five, Sec one works again, and the stored vesicles fuse.
scenes.caption: So at 37 °C, vesicles still bud and pile up. Back at 25 °C, Sec1 works again, and the stored vesicles fuse.
scenes.visual: Thermometer to '37 °C' RED: the Sec1 symbols turn RED and stall, vesicles keep budding ('budding' lamp GREEN) and pile inside the cell near the surface (no attachment shown), gauge rises. Thermometer to '25 °C': symbols turn PURPLE again, the piled vesicles fuse one after another, ORANGE dots spill outside, gauge falls.
scenes.narration: So at 37 °C, vesicles still bud and pile up. Back at 25 °C, Sec1 works again, and the stored vesicles fuse.

scenes.tts: But the pile alone never named fusion. A failed Rab, tether or SNARE for that step gives the same pile. Sec one's known job names it.
scenes.caption: But the pile alone never named fusion. A failed Rab, tether or SNARE for that step gives the same pile. Sec1's known job names it.
scenes.visual: At '37 °C' the RED fault mark hops from the TEAL Rab flag, to a tether rod, to a PURPLE SNARE rod; each time the gauge shows the same intracellular vesicle buildup, with docking left unshown (caught or uncaught is unknown). Then the mark settles on the symbol labelled 'Sec1'.
scenes.narration: But the pile alone never named fusion. A failed Rab, tether or SNARE for that step gives the same pile. Sec1's known job names it.

scenes.tts: On a linear route, cargo piles up in the last place it reached. Double mutants used that rule to put the steps in order.
scenes.visual: Whole cell. A RED block appears at the ER exit: ORANGE cargo piles inside the ER and the surface stays empty. A second RED block appears at the surface: nothing changes, the pile stays in the ER (the earlier block wins). Label 'pile = last place reached'.
scenes.narration: On a linear route, cargo piles up in the last place it reached. Double mutants used that rule to put the steps in order.

scenes.tts: Test tubes add timing. G D I, which pulls GDP-bound Rabs off membranes, blocks fusion when added at the start. What if it is added after vesicles dock?
scenes.caption: Test tubes add timing. GDI, which pulls GDP-bound Rabs off membranes, blocks fusion when added at the start. What if it is added after vesicles dock?
scenes.visual: The dashed 'cell-free' outline returns around the ER and Golgi; the gauge slot now shows a clock dial marked 'schematic' that starts ticking. At time zero, PINK GDI cups drop in and pull GREY GDP-badged TEAL flags off membranes; vesicles stay undocked and unfused near the Golgi; 'fusion' lamp RED. Reset. Question card: 'GDI added after docking?'
scenes.narration: Test tubes add timing. GDI, which pulls GDP-bound Rabs off membranes, blocks fusion when added at the start. What if it is added after vesicles dock?

scenes.visual: Predict pause. Question card stays. The clock hand sweeps; vesicles drift toward the Golgi and are caught by tether rods (docked) while the card waits.

scenes.tts: Its effect fades. Once vesicles had docked, fusion was no longer sensitive to G D I. A fast, specific inhibitor stops working once the state it targets is past.
scenes.caption: Its effect fades. Once vesicles had docked, fusion was no longer sensitive to GDI. A fast, specific inhibitor stops working once the state it targets is past.
scenes.visual: The clock passes the docking point; vesicles sit tethered at the Golgi under lit TEAL flags. PINK GDI cups now dropped in bounce off the lit flags, and the docked vesicles fuse anyway; 'fusion' lamp GREEN. Label 'GDI-sensitive step: passed'.
scenes.narration: Its effect fades. Once vesicles had docked, fusion was no longer sensitive to GDI. A fast, specific inhibitor stops working once the state it targets is past.

scenes.tts: So each vesicle on this route relies on three separate handoffs: bud, catch, fuse. Any one can fail on its own. Where cargo stalls, and when an inhibitor stops mattering, help place the break.
scenes.visual: Dashed outline and clock fade; the gauge returns. Whole cell at '25 °C': vesicles stream ER to Golgi to surface and the three lamps blink GREEN in rhythm. First the 'budding' lamp flickers RED: cargo stays in the donor and no vesicles form; it turns GREEN and flow resumes. Then 'targeting' and 'fusion' flicker RED together under one bracket: vesicles pile up inside the cell; they turn GREEN and the pile clears.
scenes.narration: So each vesicle on this route relies on three separate handoffs: bud, catch, fuse. Any one can fail on its own. Where cargo stalls, and when an inhibitor stops mattering, help place the break.

scenes.visual: End card
scenes.line: Bud, catch, fuse: three handoffs, and each can fail alone.
